annotationRationale: The solution classifies all allowable left-right patterns, counts distinct shoe permutations within each pattern, and adds the disjoint cases.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official solution using the eight allowable L/R patterns. Added a run-length argument proving the list is exhaustive and explained how boundary matches determine the shoe assignments.

review.mathCheck: An internal one-letter run would force one shoe to match two others. The resulting exhaustive two-, three-, and four-run cases contain 2, 4, and 2 patterns, contributing \(24+24+12=60\). Every boundary constraint is satisfied. Choice A is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA #20's first approach on page 10. It retains the eight patterns and their counts while supplying an explicit run-length proof of exhaustiveness.
review.annotationCheck: The direct concepts match the disjoint cases and within-case permutations. The explanation establishes both completeness and absence of duplicate counting.
